title: How to create a frame in Figma on Mac: the Frame tool, presets and shortcuts
metaTitle: How to Create a Frame in Figma on Mac: Step by Step
description: How to create a frame in Figma on Mac: press F or click the Frame tool, click or drag the canvas, then pick a preset in the right sidebar.
targetKeyword: how to create a frame in figma on mac
intro: To create a frame in Figma on Mac, press F or click the second icon in the toolbar, which is the Frame tool. Then click the canvas for a default frame, or drag to set your own width and height.
tldr: Press F or click the Frame tool, the second icon in the toolbar.
Click the canvas for a default frame, or drag for a custom size.
Pick a preset from the right sidebar while the Frame tool is active.
Use ⌥⌘G to wrap selected layers in a new frame, and ⌘D to duplicate one.

blocks.text: A frame is a container in Figma. Screens, cards, buttons and slides all sit inside frames. A top-level frame sits directly on the canvas. A nested frame sits inside another frame, such as a card inside a settings page. Frames are the base for exporting, prototyping and layout, so it pays to make them correctly from the start.
Check your Mac and Figma version first

The Figma desktop app for Mac needs macOS 12 Monterey, released in October 2021, or later. It runs on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Figma's help guide also says that each desktop app version stops being supported six months after release. If your copy is old, update it before you follow these steps, so your screen matches the instructions.

items: Open the Apple menu and choose About this Mac to see your macOS version.
That screen shows macOS, not the Figma version. The help guide gives no Figma menu path for the app version.
The desktop app matches the browser version feature for feature, so frame tools work the same way.
Desktop-only extras include pinned tabs, split tab view and multiple windows.

blocks.text: Click the canvas to make a default frame

A single click is the fastest way to make a frame, and it is the step that surprises most people. The first top-level frame in a session is 100 × 100. Figma then uses the size of your last top-level frame for the next click. So the size you get depends on what you made before, not on a fixed setting. Check the width and height before you add content, because resizing a frame with layers inside takes more effort.

blocks.title: Name before you fill
blocks.text: Name and size a frame before you add layers to it. A clear frame name is much easier to set at this stage than after the layers are placed.
Drag to set a custom size

Dragging gives you control from the first moment. Press and hold on the canvas, move diagonally to the size you want, then let go. If your drag is short, the frame ends up small. Zoom out first when the target size is larger than your screen. You can still change the size afterward, so you do not need an exact size on the first try.
Use a frame preset from the right sidebar

Presets save you from looking up device sizes. With the Frame tool active, the right sidebar shows presets under an expandable section. Figma sorts them into categories: Phone, Tablet, Desktop, Presentation, Watch, Paper, Social Media, Figma Community and Archive. Each preset adds a new frame to the canvas, and you can rename it right away.

items: Phone for a mobile app screen or a mobile web layout.
Tablet for a layout meant for a tablet screen.
Desktop for a laptop or monitor layout.
Social Media for posts that go into a feed.

blocks.text: Wrap existing layers in a new frame

Sometimes the frame comes after the drawing. Say you have a title, a photo and a button on the canvas. Select all three, then press ⌥⌘G. Figma wraps them in a new frame, and the three layers move together from then on. Windows uses Ctrl Alt G for the same action. The help article gives no Object or right-click menu path for it, so learn the shortcut.
Duplicate and quick-add frames in a flow

Press ⌘D to duplicate a selected frame when the new screen shares most of its design. With the Frame tool enabled, hover over a frame and click the + on either side to add a neighbor. Hold Option while you click + to add a blank frame of the same size. Quick-add is a fast way to lay out a row of screens without resizing each one.
Worked example: a three-screen sign-up flow

Say you are mapping a sign-up flow for a phone app with three screens: welcome, email and confirmation. Press F, expand the presets section in the right sidebar, and open the Phone category. Choose a preset, then press ⌘R and name the frame Welcome. Hover over it, click the + on the right, and name the next frame Email.

Repeat once more for Confirmation. If the Email screen needs the same header as Welcome, press ⌘D on Welcome, rename the copy and then edit it. Option-click + is for a blank screen that matches the size of the one next to it. Use each tool for the job it does best, and you will spend less time resizing.
Name frames so you can find them later

Frames get lost fast in a large file. Rename each frame as soon as you make it. Select it and press ⌘R, or double-click the name in the Layers panel. Use names that say what the screen is, such as Login, Login error or Settings Profile. Good names also make exports and handoffs easier to read.
Use zoom shortcuts to find a frame

After you create a frame, press ⇧1 to zoom to fit the whole page, or ⇧2 to zoom to the selection. Those two shortcuts help when a frame lands off screen. The [zoom guide on this site](/how-to/zoom-in-and-out-in-figma) covers the trackpad and mouse options if you prefer those.
Common mistakes that waste time

items: Clicking inside a frame by accident, which makes a small nested frame instead of a new top-level one.
Pressing F while a text box is active, so nothing happens.
Waiting for a size dialog. Figma's help article describes no dialog for frame creation.
Leaving frames unnamed, which makes later exports harder to sort.
Running a desktop build older than six months after its release, which Figma no longer supports.

blocks.text: When a new frame does not show up on the canvas

Some people report a frame that appears in Preview but not on the canvas. In an October 2023 community thread, the suggested first step was to double-click the frame's # icon in the Layers panel. That zooms to the frame. Figma staff could not reproduce the problem. They suggested updating your browser, reinstalling the desktop app, and restarting. That thread has no Mac-specific steps and no recorded outcome, so treat it as a starting point, not a fix.

blocks.title: Check the thread date
blocks.text: The thread dates from October 2023. Figma's app has changed since then, so the exact steps people described may not match your version.
What the latest Figma releases change

I checked the April 29, 2026 and May 1, 2026 release notes. Neither changes how you create a frame. The April note adds an Add reference button to almost any canvas node, frames included, for AI image generation and editing. The May note adds tab search in the overflow menu and lets Mac users open Figma links directly in the desktop app.
Where to go next

Selecting layers for ⌥⌘G is faster from the keyboard, as the [keyboard selection guide](/how-to/select-layers-with-the-keyboard-in-figma) explains. Once you have a frame, the usual next step is layout. The guide on [adding auto layout in Figma on Mac](/how-to/add-auto-layout-in-figma) shows how a frame can arrange its children. When a screen is ready to share, [export a frame as PNG in Figma on Mac](/how-to/export-a-frame-as-png-in-figma) covers the file output step.

faq.question: Which macOS version do I need for Figma on Mac?
faq.answer: Figma's help guide lists macOS 12 Monterey, released in October 2021, as the minimum. The desktop app runs on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. To see your macOS version, open the Apple menu and choose About this Mac.

faq.question: Why is my first frame 100 × 100?
faq.answer: Figma sets the first top-level frame in each session to 100 × 100. Later top-level frames copy the size of the last one you made. Drag if you want a specific size from the start.

faq.question: Is there a menu item to create a frame?
faq.answer: Figma's help article describes the Frame tool and its shortcuts. It describes no dialog for frame creation and gives no Object or right-click menu path for these actions. Use the toolbar or the F key.

faq.question: Do the desktop app and the browser version make frames the same way?
faq.answer: Yes. Figma says the desktop app offers the same features as the browser version. Desktop-only extras include pinned tabs, split tab view and multiple windows.

faq.question: What is the Windows shortcut for wrapping layers in a frame?
faq.answer: Figma's help article gives Ctrl Alt G for Windows, where the Mac shortcut is Option Command G. This guide does not cover other Windows keys, so check the keyboard shortcuts panel in the app.

faq.question: Did recent Figma releases change how frames work?
faq.answer: The April 29, 2026 and May 1, 2026 release notes do not change how you create a frame. They add an Add reference button on canvas nodes and tab search in the overflow menu, among other changes.

faq.question: Can I rename a frame after I create it?
faq.answer: Yes. Select the frame and press ⌘R to rename its layer. Give frames clear names before you export them, so the files are easy to tell apart.

task: Create a frame in Figma on Mac
appliesTo: Figma desktop app for Mac on macOS 12 or later, Intel and Apple silicon
requirements: A Mac running macOS 12 Monterey or later
The Figma desktop app for Mac, or the browser version
Edit access to the Figma file you want to change
Keyboard focus on the canvas, not inside a text box

steps.name: Open the file you want to edit
steps.text: Open the Figma desktop app, then open the design file you want to change. New frames land on the canvas of the open file, so check the file name before you click.
steps.tip: If the file is view only, you cannot add frames. Ask the file owner for edit access.

steps.name: Select the Frame tool
steps.text: Click the second icon in the toolbar, or press F. Figma's help article also lists A as a shortcut, but the third-party shortcut lists show only F.
steps.tip: If F does nothing, click an empty spot on the canvas first, then press F again.

steps.name: Click the canvas for a default frame
steps.text: Click an empty spot on the canvas. The first top-level frame in a session is 100 × 100. Later clicks copy the size of the last top-level frame you made.
steps.tip: Read the width and height before you add any content to the frame.

steps.name: Or drag to set a custom size
steps.text: Press and hold on the canvas, drag diagonally to the size you want, then let go. Dragging sets custom dimensions instead of the default size.
steps.tip: Zoom out first if the frame needs to be bigger than your screen.

steps.name: Pick a preset from the right sidebar
steps.text: Keep the Frame tool active. In the right sidebar, click the arrow to expand the presets section. Open a category such as Desktop, then choose a preset. Figma adds the new frame to the canvas.
steps.tip: Presets only show while the Frame tool is active. Select the Frame tool again if the list is missing.

steps.name: Nest a frame inside another frame
steps.text: Click inside an existing frame to add a nested frame. A nested frame also starts at 100 × 100. Click and drag inside the parent to choose its size.
steps.tip: If you meant a top-level frame, click outside the parent first.

steps.name: Wrap existing layers in a frame
steps.text: Select the layers you want inside. Press ⌥⌘G to wrap them in a new frame. The help article gives no menu path for this action, so use the shortcut.
steps.tip: Windows uses Ctrl Alt G for the same action.

steps.name: Duplicate a frame
steps.text: Select the frame, then press ⌘D to duplicate it. Edit the copy, not the original, when the new screen shares a layout with the old one.
steps.tip: Rename the copy straight away, so you can tell the two apart.

steps.name: Quick-add a frame beside another
steps.text: With the Frame tool enabled, hover over a frame. Click the + on either side to add a frame there. Hold Option while you click + to add a blank frame of the same size.
steps.tip: Use quick-add for a row of screens, then check each frame's size.

steps.name: Rename the frame
steps.text: Select the frame and press ⌘R to rename its layer. If ⌘R does nothing, double-click the name in the Layers panel, then type the new name.
steps.tip: Use names that describe the screen, such as Login or Settings.

troubleshooting.problem: The frame shows in Preview but not on the canvas
troubleshooting.fix: Double-click the frame's # icon in the Layers panel to zoom to it. If it still does not appear, quit Figma and reopen it. A 2023 community thread has no Mac-specific fix, so contact Figma support if this keeps happening.

troubleshooting.problem: The new frame is tiny and sits inside another frame
troubleshooting.fix: You clicked inside a parent frame, which makes a 100 × 100 nested frame. Click outside the parent, or drag the frame into place.

troubleshooting.problem: New frames are the wrong size
troubleshooting.fix: Later clicks copy the size of the last top-level frame. Drag for a custom size, or choose a preset from the right sidebar.
A text box or another field may have focus. Click an empty spot on the canvas, then press F again.

troubleshooting.problem: The presets section is missing from the sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: Presets show only while the Frame tool is active. Select the Frame tool, then expand the presets section with its arrow.

troubleshooting.problem: A shortcut in this guide does not work on your Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Open the keyboard shortcuts panel in Figma. See [how to show keyboard shortcuts in Figma on Mac](/how-to/show-the-keyboard-shortcuts-panel-in-figma). Third-party lists can differ from your version.
